body:
A hockey puck is moved between two points on a rough horizontal surface, once along a straight line and once along a longer curved path. Kinetic friction acts on the puck the whole time. Which statement about the work done on the puck by friction is correct?

Choices:
A. The work is the same on both paths, because the endpoints are the same.
B. The work is zero on both paths, because the surface is horizontal.
C. The work is larger in magnitude along the longer curved path.
D. The work is positive on both paths, because the friction force is pushing along the surface.

A ball is thrown straight up, rises, and falls back to the height of the hand that threw it. Air resistance is not negligible. Which statement describes the net work done on the ball over the whole trip?

Choices:
A. Gravity does negative net work, and air resistance does zero net work.
B. Gravity does zero net work, and air resistance does negative net work.
C. Both gravity and air resistance do zero net work, because the ball returns to its starting height.
D. Both gravity and air resistance do negative net work, because both oppose the upward motion.

A crate is moved from the bottom of a rough ramp to a platform at the top by two different routes: a short straight slide and a long, winding slide. Both start and end at the same two points. Which statement is correct?

Choices:
A. The work done by gravity is the same for both routes, but the work done by friction is not.
B. The work done by gravity and the work done by friction are both the same for both routes.
C. The work done by friction is the same for both routes, but the work done by gravity is not.
D. The work done by gravity and the work done by friction both differ between the routes.
